question: Should the bundled coding-agent skill intentionally fail closed for every Git-backed edit when canonical remote provenance or launcher-prepared worktree verification cannot be established?
rationale: The stricter rule improves reproducibility and trust isolation but can deliberately stop previously permitted delegated workflows; documentation checks cannot decide whether that compatibility tradeoff is the desired product policy.

options.title: Confirm strict fail-closed policy
options.body: Accept the new launch contract as intentional and refresh the branch against current main before merge.

options.title: Preserve a trusted-checkout exception
options.body: Narrow the rule to permit an explicitly verified trusted existing checkout when fresh canonical worktree preparation is unavailable.

options.title: Pause for broader workflow design
options.body: Defer the PR until maintainers define one repository-wide delegated-coding trust and worktree contract beyond this bundled skill.

recommendation.title: Confirm strict fail-closed policy
recommendation.body: Accept the new launch contract as intentional and refresh the branch against current main before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The file history shows the strongest and most recent ownership of coding-agent workflow and safety policy.
